objective: Make every dynamic text path in Pi-Bolt's `bench/report.py` SVG output XML-safe, so user- or metadata-supplied labels cannot inject SVG elements, attributes, or scripts, without changing the visuals of ordinary inputs.

evidence: Inventory of insertion sites recorded in final report.
esc() helper added; all 13 dynamic sites escaped; tspan markup preserved; dataset output byte-identical to HEAD.
10 unittest cases pass, including injection payloads, Unicode, already-escaped text, XML parse validation.
Tests green; 12 dataset SVGs and 12 attack-label SVGs parse; README note added.

report:
I'll audit the actual repository state against the objective.

Audit findings:

- Inspected `bench/report.py`: `esc()` uses `xml.sax.saxutils.escape` with `"`/`'`, strips XML 1.0-invalid characters before escaping, and is applied at every dynamic SVG write site: chart title/subtitle/aria-label, panel names, build labels, values and ratio notes; hero title/subtitle/aria-label, tile names, large figure and unit `tspan`, comparison lines, build labels and values.
- Ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench -p 'test_report.py' -v`: all 10 tests pass, including injection payloads, attribute breakout, Unicode, invalid control characters, escaped-looking input, and tspan preservation.
- Independently regenerated the 12 SVGs for `bench/results/2026-10-10-pi-bolt-0.7.3` with the changed script versus `git HEAD`'s script: SVGs and tables byte-identical. I also compared 20 other results directories: all identical. One unrelated directory fails identically in both versions due to a pre-existing empty-values error.
- Ran end-to-end malicious `--label` and `--builds` payloads plus a crafted metadata `pauses.jsonl` step name: all 12 SVGs parse as XML, contain no `<script>` or injected elements/attributes, and render the payload as literal text without double-escaping.
- Documentation in `bench/README.md` accurately describes the guarantee and test command. The new test file is present but currently untracked; that is not a functional gap in the objective.

The escaping is complete at the actual SVG insertion sites, adversarial and ordinary inputs behave as required, and the stated objective is satisfied.
